systems_found: Stephen F. Austin State University (now in UT System)
Texas public community college districts (about 50, each locally governed; no statewide system payroll)

sources.institution: Texas College Salaries (volunteer project, data from Texas Public Information Act requests)
sources.system: Multi-system: UT, Texas A&M, Texas Tech, UH, UNT, Texas State, TWU, TSTC, about 25 community college districts
sources.coverage_years: 2020-2026 (snapshots; latest data dates 2025-01 to 2026-06 depending on institution)
sources.institutions_covered: 67 institutions (universities, health science centers, system offices, community colleges), 181,913 employees on file
sources.employees: all (as released by each institution; annual base salary only)
sources.format: CSV (Google Drive file 'TCS Export 05_25_2026.csv', plus a Google Doc readme); HTML per-employee pages on the site
sources.terms: Search results say the site is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0; FAQ says data come from TPIA requests and are not sold
sources.notes: This is the best single bulk source for Texas public higher ed. It is unofficial and volunteer-run. Fields vary by institution because each school answers the records request differently (FAQ Q03). Base salary only, no overtime or supplemental pay. The download is a Google Drive folder, so you need the file ID or Drive API to fetch it automatically. A 'Data processing statement' page describes how the data were cleaned. I did not download the CSV, so the fields listed are inferred from the FAQ and site pages.

sources.institution: Texas Tribune Government Salaries Explorer (Texas Comptroller state employee payroll)
sources.coverage_years: Snapshot 2026-07-01 (older snapshots probably exist at the same S3 prefix)
sources.institutions_covered: 116 state agencies; public universities and colleges are NOT included
sources.employees: all state agency employees (not higher ed)
sources.terms: not stated (Tribune publishes it in the public interest)
sources.blocker: Leaves out institutions of higher education; useful only as a template or for any A&M System service agencies, if they are included
sources.notes: Clean A-quality file for state agencies, rated D here because it has no university payroll. The Tribune says it 'no longer publishes salaries for other employees'. Its 2010-2011 higher-ed data (UT, A&M, Tech, UH, UNT) is no longer published. I could not confirm whether A&M System agencies such as AgriLife Extension, Forest Service or TEEX appear in it.

sources.institution: UT System institutional annual operating budgets
sources.system: University of Texas System (also Stephen F. Austin)
sources.coverage_years: FY2019-FY2027 (older volumes on UNT Portal to Texas History)
sources.blocker: Not person-level: totals by department and salary category only
sources.notes: I checked the SFA FY2027 volume (116 pages). It has department totals for FTE and salaries but no names. Recorded so nobody re-checks it.

sources.institution: OpenPayrolls / GovSalaries / OpenTheBooks (commercial or nonprofit aggregators)
sources.terms: not stated (openpayrolls.com returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch)
sources.blocker: Search-only third-party sites; openpayrolls blocks automated access (403); no bulk download
sources.notes: Secondary sources. Texas College Salaries is better.

private_extra: None found. Rice, SMU, Baylor, TCU and other Texas privates publish only IRS 990 data.
gaps: There is no official statewide or system-level person-level higher-ed payroll file. The Comptroller payroll leaves out universities, and UT, A&M and Tech budgets are aggregate. Universities do not post person-level salaries on their own sites, so Texas depends on the volunteer TPIA-based Texas College Salaries dataset. It covers about 25 of roughly 50 community college districts and base salary only (no total or other pay).
notes: I treated the Tribune/Comptroller file as out of scope for universities (rated D) but recorded it because it is clean and bulk. I checked UT System operating budget PDFs and confirmed they are aggregate. I did not download the Texas College Salaries CSV (22.5 MB), so its fields come from the FAQ and site pages. The best fix for official data would be TPIA requests to each system office.
